doc.title: Louie Bellson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

title: Working with Joe Williams and professional singers
summary: Joe Williams, Tony Bennett and others rehearse efficiently, unlike difficult performers, per Johnny Carson.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: Have you ever had occasion to play with Joe Williams?

Joe Williams? Absolutely. There is an example, well he’s such a great talent, but what makes Joe Williams so great, is not only is he one of the greatest singers in the world, but when he comes in to rehearse, he comes in like a gentleman, he knows exactly what he wants to rehearse, what he wants to work out, he does it, he’s in and out with no problems. That to me is a real artist you know? Because he knows exactly what the band should sound like, what the dynamic should be, what he wants from the drummer, and he does it in a relationship like a love relationship. “Here, let’s all work together and get this thing going.” He does it, in and out. I love working with him. Tony Bennett is another guy like that. Basie was the same way, Ellington. Those kind of performers, they know exactly what they want to do. never had trouble with the biggies. Ella Fitzgerald would come on the show, Joe Williams, Tony Bennett, Duke, whoever it was, Dizzy. In and out. It was always that person that didn’t quite make it that — “something is wrong with the dressing room.”
“I don’t have room in the dressing room” — something — “the band’s too loud.” And of course that’s the last time you saw them on the show.
